evaluator.name: Irregular (formerly Pattern Labs)
evaluator.hq: Tel Aviv, IL / San Francisco, US
evaluator.summary: Offensive-cyber evaluator cited in OpenAI and Anthropic system cards; SOLVE framework used by UK AISI. Pattern Labs and Irregular are the same company.
evaluator.what_would_move_the_score: A published COI policy, disclosure of lab revenue share, and a firewall between evaluations and the security-products business.

dissent.lower: Role incompatibility (1 to 0). Irregular says it works side by side with OpenAI and Anthropic 'to develop the defenses needed before deployment' and describes a roadmap of runtime security controls for the same customers it evaluates. If any evaluated lab pays for those defenses, X.1 places the company at 0: it would be selling the fix to the party it grades.
dissent.higher: Funding (1 to 2). The revenue disclosed is 'millions' from lab partnerships, but the UK government uses the SOLVE framework and the company markets to enterprises beyond the labs. If a non-lab revenue base is documented, per-engagement lab fees beside that base cap at 2 under F.3 rather than 1 under F.5.

F.rationale: Anchor 1: a $6.8M Coefficient Giving grant appears in the index under the former name Pattern Labs (irregular.11; ledger T09 marked differs, unreconciled). A name-search under ‘Irregular’ found nothing (irregular.12), which does not rebut the old-name row — the project treats the two names as the same company. Material lab-adjacent funding with disputed attribution.
open_questions: Re-run the Coefficient index search under both Irregular and Pattern Labs and record the snapshot.
